record.paper_title: The Hamiltonian Seifert Conjecture: Examples and Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist a proper smooth Hamiltonian system in dimension four with a regular compact energy level that carries no periodic orbit? More specifically, if one starts from G. Kuperberg's C^1 divergence-free vector field on S^3 without periodic orbits, can that vector field be realized as the characteristic flow coming from a C^2 embedding, or even a C^1 embedding, of S^3 into R^4? A positive answer would produce a C^2 Hamiltonian counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

evidence.quote: Neither the method from [Gi2, Gi5] nor from [Her3] apply to four-dimensional manifolds. There are also serious difficulties in adapting Kuperberg's plug, [KuK1], to the symplectic setting. A C1-smooth divergence–free vector field on S3 was found by G. Kuperberg, [KuG]. It is not known whether or not this vector field can be obtained by a C2- (or even C1-) embedding of S3 into R4. Such an embedding would give a C2-smooth "counterexample" to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. A smooth Hamiltonian system on $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ is the flow generated by a smooth function $H\colon \mathbb{R}^{2n}	o\mathbb{R}$ with respect to the standard symplectic form $\omega_0 = \sum_{i=1}^{n} dx_i\wedge dy_i$, i.e. the flow of the vector field $X_H$ defined by $\iota_{X_H}\omega_0 = -dH$. A value $c\in\mathbb{R}$ is regular if $dH
eq 0$ on $H^{-1}(c)$, and $H$ is called proper if preimages of compact sets are compact. On a regular compact energy level $\Sigma = H^{-1}(c)$ the Hamiltonian flow is, up to time reparametrization, the characteristic foliation determined by $\ker(\omega_0|_\Sigma)$; in particular, when $\Sigma$ is a smooth hypersurface in $\mathbb{R}^4$ this characteristic foliation is a one-dimensional foliation depending only on the embedding of $\Sigma$.

G. Kuperberg has constructed a $C^1$-smooth divergence-free (i.e. volume-preserving) vector field $V$ on $S^3$ having no periodic orbits.

Problem. (a) Does there exist a proper smooth Hamiltonian function $H\colon \mathbb{R}^4	o\mathbb{R}$ admitting a regular compact energy level on which the Hamiltonian flow has no periodic orbit?

(b) More specifically, can Kuperberg's $C^1$ divergence-free vector field on $S^3$ be realized, up to reparametrization, as the characteristic flow of a $C^2$-embedding (or even a $C^1$-embedding) of $S^3$ into $\mathbb{R}^4$ equipped with the standard symplectic form? A positive answer would yield a $C^2$-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four.
artifact.status_search_result: The general existence question (a) — a $C^2$-smooth proper Hamiltonian on $\mathbb{R}^4$ with a regular compact energy level carrying no periodic orbit — was resolved affirmatively by Ginzburg and Gürel (Annals of Mathematics, 2003), who constructed a $C^2$-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in $\mathbb{R}^4$. Their construction does not proceed by embedding Kuperberg's $S^3$ vector field into $\mathbb{R}^4$, so the more specific realization question (b) appears to remain open. The smoothness gap (no $C^\infty$ counterexample in dimension four is known) also remains open.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R^4
status_evidence.snippet: We construct a proper C^2-smooth function on R^4 such that its Hamiltonian flow has no periodic orbits on at least one regular level set.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of a C^2 Hamiltonian counterexample in dimension four was established by Ginzburg and Gürel.

status_evidence.title: A C^2-smooth counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in R^4 (Annals of Mathematics)
status_evidence.claim: The result was published in Annals of Mathematics in 2003.

status_evidence.title: Seifert conjecture - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Ginzburg and Gürel constructed a C^2 counterexample to the Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four; smoother versions remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The smooth (C^infty) Hamiltonian Seifert conjecture in dimension four remains open.
